explanation: In C++, template functions allow writing generic functions that can operate with different data types without rewriting code for each type. By specifying type parameters, such as 'class' or 'typename', templates enable compile-time polymorphism, leading to more flexible and reusable code. This is especially useful in the Standard Template Library (STL) and modern C++ idioms, where generic algorithms and data structures are prevalent.
syntax:
template <class TypeParameter1, class TypeParameter2, ...>
ReturnType FunctionName(Parameters);
